"This group is long overdue," said Carruthers. "We believe that science
used to guide public policy decisions should be based on sound principles -- not

on emotions and beliefs considered by some as 'politically correct'. Too often,
public policy decisions that are based on inadequate science impose enormous
economic costs and other hardships on consumers, businesses and government.
It's time we expose this problem more vigilantly, and alert the public to the
rapidly rising costs of regulations coming from these policies."
TASSC currently has over 300 members including scientists and
representatives from universities and independent organizations and industry.
Formed recently, TASSC has already obtained broad-based national support.
"Compliance with environmental regulations cost the nation an incredible
$115 billion in 199l alone. And we agree that government regulations are needed
for enforcing legitimate guidelines, " said Carruthers. "But as a former professor
of agriculture economics, I am acutely aware of proper scientific guidelines --
guidelines written years ago and still valid today -- that are being cast aside to
make science 'fit' with the political leanings of special interests. The cost to us
is simply too high to see this disturbing trend continue."
